newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS - Argentaria raises Telefonica stake.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Argentaria raises Telefonica stake.

text.p: Spain's Argentaria raised its stake in Telefonica de Espana to more than five percent just weeks before the telecommunication group's full privatisation and said it did not rule out further purchases.

"(The bank) is betting on the group's future and does not rule out increasing its participation since Argentaria at the moment has a surplus of funds of more than 260 billion pesetas ($2 billion)," Argentaria spokesman Manuel Bueno told Reuters on Wednesday.
Late on Tuesday, Argentaria bought 20 million Telefonica shares, at 3,170 pesetas each, for 63.4 billion pesetas.

Telefonica shares -- which have already risen 80 percent in the past year -- jumped nearly 4.5 percent on Wednesday morning to a high of 3,310 after news Argentaria had increased its stake by 2.12 percent to a total 5.21 percent.

The purchase ensures Argentaria's place at the heart of Telefonica's core shareholders alongside Spain's second-largest bank Banco Bilbao Vizcaya (BBV) and huge Catalonian savings bank La Caixa, each of which own some five percent.

The three financial groups, together with Morgan Stanley, are the global coordinators for Spain's sale of its remaining Telefonica stake of 21.01 percent. The final number and price of the shares, due in the coming weeks, has yet to be set.
For Argentaria, the larger stake gives it favourable tax treatment, while also ensuring it has equal control over Spain's largest company with the other, bigger shareholders.

"Everone believes that you have to be in Telefonica and Argentaria doesn't want to be left behind. The bank has decided to even up its stake with those of the other shareholders," one Madrid-based analyst said.
At 3,170 pesetas a share, analysts called the price high. In addition, Argentaria will need to amortise some 30 billion pesetas in goodwill, slightly diluting earnings.
But analysts added that with the larger stake Argentaria may now deduct 100 percent of its dividends from taxes by using the so-called equity-accounting method.
If BBV continues to up its stake, Argentaria is likely to try to keep pace although the tremendous financial solidity of its fellow shareholders may make this difficult despite its ample cash.
"Argentaria isn't going to renounce a position of control in Spain's largest company for say, one percent," said Juan Berberana, analyst at AB Asesores.
BBV considers Telefonica a key strategic holding given the major presence of both groups in Latin America.
A spokesman for La Caixa told Reuters that "at the moment we are content as we are (with Telefonica)."

Telefonica president Juan Villalonga recently encouraged the core shareholders, set up at the government's instigation in February 1995, to raise their collective stake to 25 percent. He suggested a 10 percent stake for la Caixa and for BBV and five percent for Argentaria.
